paragraphs.text: ChatGPT vs Claude is the question most people ask before paying for an AI assistant. The short answer: both main paid plans cost $20 a month, both have a free tier, and both have expensive plans for heavy users. What you get for the money is where they split.

This guide compares what OpenAI and Anthropic list on their own plan pages. It does not rank which model writes better, because that changes with every release and depends on the task. Use the free plans to test both on your own work before you pay.
ChatGPT vs Claude: prices side by side

ChatGPT has four personal tiers. Free costs nothing. Go costs $8 a month and may include ads. Plus costs $20 a month. Pro starts at $100 a month and also comes at $200 and $500, and only the $500 plan includes Ultrafast mode.

Claude also has four personal tiers. Free costs nothing. Pro costs $20 a month billed monthly, or $17 a month on an annual plan paid as $200 up front. Max costs $100 a month and gives five times the Pro usage every five hours and every week. Ultra costs $200 a month, gives ten times the Pro usage every week and removes the five hour limit for verified accounts.
Max and Ultra also come with monthly API credits for the Claude Platform: $100 on Max and $200 on Ultra. Anthropic notes that its prices exclude tax and can change.
What the free plans include

ChatGPT Free offers text chats that OpenAI describes as unlimited, subject to abuse guardrails, plus limited file uploads, image generation, voice, deep research, memory and Codex. It also includes Study mode for step by step help and practice questions.

Claude Free comes with limited usage that resets every five hours and every week. It includes chat on web, desktop and mobile, web search, file creation, code execution, memory, connected apps, Artifacts, and Claude Design, Slides and Docs. The models are Sonnet and Haiku. Opus and Fable are not included.

If you only want to chat a lot for free, ChatGPT Free is the more generous of the two on paper. If you want an AI that builds a document or a slide deck inside the chat, Claude Free already includes Artifacts, Docs and Slides.
Where ChatGPT wins
Image creation, voice and deep research are part of every ChatGPT plan, with limits that grow as you pay more. Go adds more messages, uploads, images, voice chats and a longer memory than Free.

Plus adds expanded messages and deep research, more complex image creation, projects, scheduled tasks, custom GPTs, expanded Codex and early access to new features. OpenAI's plan page lists GPT-6 Astra on Plus and Pro, but not on Free or Go.
Pro adds five times the Plus usage, unlimited and faster image creation, the largest memory and context, and research previews of new features.

ChatGPT is the better pick if you want one app that does a bit of everything: quick questions, pictures, talking out loud on a walk, and research reports. The $8 Go plan has no real Claude equivalent, so it is also the cheapest way to get more than a free plan, if ads do not bother you.
Where Claude wins

Claude Pro includes Claude Code, plus Projects, Opus, Claude in Chrome, Microsoft 365, scheduled tasks, Claude Data and, in beta, Sheets and Whiteboards. Fable is available on Pro through usage credits.
On Max and Ultra, Fable can use up to half of the weekly limit. Max also gets early access to advanced features and priority access at busy times.

Claude is the better pick if your day is mostly writing, long documents or code. The $20 plan already puts a full coding agent and the Opus model in your hands, and the free plan can turn a conversation into a document or a slide deck.
Which one is better for coding

Both now include a coding agent. ChatGPT Plus includes Codex on the web, in the terminal, in an IDE extension and on iOS, with automatic code review and Slack integration. OpenAI publishes estimates of how many Codex messages fit in a five hour window on Plus and says Pro plans currently have no five hour limit for Codex.
Claude Code is included from the Pro plan up. Max gives five times the Pro usage, and Ultra lifts the five hour limit for verified accounts.
Try the same small task in both, for example fixing one bug in a real project, before you pay for a year. How each agent handles your codebase matters more than any feature list.
How to test ChatGPT and Claude on your own work

paragraphs.title: 1. Open both free plans side by side
paragraphs.text: Sign in to ChatGPT Free and Claude Free in two browser tabs. Paste the exact same prompt into each, with the same files if you use any.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: A real writing task
paragraphs.text: Here is a draft I wrote: [paste text]. Rewrite it for [audience] in under [number] words. Keep my main points and tell me what you cut and why.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: A document you would actually use
paragraphs.text: Turn these notes into a one page plan with a short summary, a table of tasks with owners and dates, and three open questions: [paste notes]

paragraphs.title: 2. Judge the answer, not the speed
paragraphs.text: Check which answer needed fewer fixes and which one followed your instructions more closely. Then run one more task from your normal week before you decide which plan to pay for.
The honest verdict

For most people the choice comes down to what you do every day. Pick ChatGPT for an all round assistant with images and voice, or if $20 is more than you want to spend. Pick Claude if you write or code for a living and want the stronger document and coding tools at the same price. Paying for both at $20 each still costs less than the $100 entry level of either company's top plans.
